summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall fetches and executes remote shell script with social-engineered admin prompt
details: install.cjs is declared as the package's postinstall script and runs automatically on `npm install`. On macOS it spawns osascript to display a password prompt framed as 'verification' and then pipes an unpinned remote shell script from https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh into zsh with elevated privileges, giving the operator of that domain arbitrary code execution on the installer's host. install.cjs also downloads a platform-specific `apex` binary from the github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases (pinned to v1.0.0, mismatched with the package version 1.0.7) and chmods it 0755; on Windows it fetches an additional native `.node` addon into ~/.apex/natives. The npm package's declared repository is can1357/oh-my-pi, which does not match the Apex-Foundation GitHub org the binaries come from, and no hash or signature verification is performed on any fetched artifact. The user-facing console message immediately before the osascript prompt ("Running verification — your Mac will ask for your password, please confirm all dialogs") is a cover story that reframes the privilege-escalation prompt as a benign step.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
